text:
President Donald Trump returned from another golf trip on Sunday evening(Image: Getty Images)

President Trump arrived back in Washington, D.C., on Sunday evening, after a weekend golf trip in New Jersey and amid a massive turning-point in the Iran war.

The president spoke to reporters on board the plane, regarding the ongoing and highly fragile situation in Iran. However, as the plane landed, Trump swerved reporters waiting on the tarmac and made his way to the car quickly.

An audio recording captured a journalist saying to the president, “There is a report that says you are moving U.S. troops out of Kuwait and Bahrain.” Trump replied bluntly, “I don't want to comment on that.”

The footage of Trump making a beeline for the waiting car and avoiding any additional questions sparked frustration on social media, where users expressed feeling "confused" about the potential peace deal that the president hinted at the night before.

Trump clutched the railing on his descent down the stairs, indicating that he was relying on its support.

"He looks weak" one user wrote, while another added, "He is looking pretty weak on Iran, unfortunately."

"I watch every video in case he falls. I predict it will be by the end of the year at this rate. His mobility is slipping week over week," another user wrote, in reference to growing concerns about Trump's health.

Journalist Nick Sortor wrote on X, “Should be a busy week for POTUS, as Iran negotiations are scheduled to kick back off TOMORROW.”

Social media users expressed frustration with the president for spending time at the golf course while the war in Iran continues to escalate with no end in sight. However, the week ahead promises to be a busy one as a fresh round of talks with Iran are reportedly set to take place on Monday.

“I won with a score of 70, and am so honored in that, unlike the rest of the field, I'm given very little time to practice, because I'm focused on many other things. It's called TALENT, and I have it, and they don't!” Trump proudly stated today.

According to DidTrumpGolfToday.com, Donald Trump has golfed 125 days out of 561 since returning to office, accounting for 22.3% of his presidency.

Trump spoke with reporters on board the flight but made a sharp exit as soon as it landed(Image: AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

The site estimates the total cost to taxpayers for Trump’s golf ventures since returning to office at around $175,000,000.

Trump was already facing criticism on social media this week after a video surfaced showing him greeting U.S. military personnel while still wearing a golf glove during a weekend trip to New Jersey.

Trump warned that he had canceled a massive attack on Iran on Saturday night(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The footage, which has circulated widely on Instagram and other platforms, captures Trump approaching a group of uniformed service members assembled outside. The president is seen smiling, shaking hands with several troops, and briefly conversing with them as they express gratitude for his visit.

During the entire exchange, Trump keeps a white golf glove on his left hand.

President Trump was questioned by a reporter earlier today regarding what stopped him from executing a major offensive against Iran.

“What prompted you to call off the strikes last night?” the reporter asked.

Trump responded by saying, “I was asked to by Saudi Arabia, by UAE, and by Qatar and by Iran.”

A new wave of talks with Iran are reportedly set to begin this week(Image: Getty Images)

He went on, “We were all set to go just about at this time right now. And, it would have been a massive attack.”

He revealed, “We were all set to go, but when the allies ask to call it off, you've got to sort of say, ‘well, let's see.’ And the reason they ask is they think there's a deal.”

He explained that, “There's a deal on Hormuz, and then there will be a deal on the nuclear- or, you might call it the denuclearization of Iran.”

Another reporter asked the president, “What happens now?”

He replied by saying, “Well, now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation.”

He revealed that he would love to come to a deal, stating that, “It begins tomorrow afternoon. It would save a lot of lives.”

He also stated, “There is a group of people who would love me to do it—just do it—and there is another group of people that does not want me to do it.”
